os_macos_intro: CowCatcher AI runs on the open-source AI Detector engine. Follow the eight steps below and your barn is being monitored live — everything runs locally on your own Mac, without a subscription.
os_macos_download_desc: Download the macOS file in the latest release.
os_macos_req_title: Before you start: what you need
os_macos_req_text: The macOS build runs on Apple Silicon Macs (M1, M2, M3, M4) as well as on Intel Macs. On an Apple Silicon Mac you can expect around 60 ms per frame at a very low power draw, which is more than fast enough for accurate detection.
os_macos_step1_title: Download the two files from GitHub
os_macos_step1_1: Open the releases page of the AI Detector project with the button above in Safari, Chrome or Firefox, or search Google for “CowCatcher AI GitHub” and click Releases.
os_macos_step1_2: Download exactly two files: the macOS engine (aidetector-osx) and the web version — the interface where you set everything up.
os_macos_step1_caption: The releases page: the macOS build (aidetector-osx) is listed under Assets.
os_macos_step2_title: Create a folder and unpack the files
os_macos_step2_1: Go to your desktop, click with two fingers on the trackpad (or right-click) and choose New Folder. Name it Cowcatcher.
os_macos_step2_2: Open Finder, go to Downloads and drag both .zip files into the Cowcatcher folder on your desktop.
os_macos_step2_3: Double-click both .zip files. macOS unpacks them automatically with Archive Utility.
os_macos_step2_4: Delete the original .zip files to keep the folder tidy.
os_macos_step3_title: Give the Mac permission to run the program
os_macos_step3_intro: CowCatcher AI does not come from the App Store and has no paid Apple developer certificate, so macOS blocks it on the first launch — with a message such as “cannot be opened because the developer cannot be verified”, “is damaged and can’t be opened” or “macOS cannot check it for malicious software”. Any of the three methods below gives permission; pick the one that suits your macOS version.
os_macos_step3_a_title: Method A — via System Settings (recommended for Ventura, Sonoma and Sequoia)
os_macos_step3_a_1: Try to open the program once by double-clicking it, then click Cancel on the security message.
os_macos_step3_a_2: Click the Apple logo in the top-left corner and open System Settings → Privacy & Security.
os_macos_step3_a_3: Scroll all the way down in the right-hand pane to Security. You see the text: “‘Cowcatcher AI’ was blocked from use because it is not from an identified developer.”
os_macos_step3_a_4: Click the button Open Anyway next to that text and confirm with your Mac password or Touch ID. Click Open on the final question.
os_macos_step3_b_2: Hold the Control key and click the program (or right-click it), then choose Open at the top of the menu.
os_macos_step3_b_3: Click Open in the security dialog. macOS remembers this choice and will start the program without warnings from now on.
os_macos_step3_c_title: Method C — via Terminal (if macOS says the file is “damaged”)
os_macos_step3_c_intro: macOS sometimes puts downloaded files in a so-called quarantine zone. You can remove that quarantine flag in five seconds:
os_macos_step3_c_1: Open Terminal (press Cmd + Space, type Terminal and press Enter).
os_macos_step3_c_2: Type the command below, including the space at the end, and then drag the Cowcatcher folder from your desktop straight into the Terminal window. The path is filled in for you.
os_macos_step3_c_3: Press <kbd>Enter</kbd> and type your Mac login password. You will not see any characters appear while typing — that is normal. Press <kbd>Enter</kbd> again.
os_macos_step3_c_4: All files in the folder are now permanently unblocked.
os_macos_keep_1: Use a network cable. Connect the Mac and the cameras with a wired connection. Using a MacBook or Mac mini without a built-in ethernet port? Then use a reliable USB-C to ethernet adapter.
os_macos_keep_2: Stop the Mac from sleeping. Open System Settings → Energy Saver (or Displays) and enable “Prevent automatic sleeping when the display is off”. A free tool such as Amphetamine or Caffeine can keep the Mac awake 24/7.
os_macos_keep_3: Start automatically at login. Go to System Settings → General → Login Items, click the + under ‘Open at Login’ and select the CowCatcher AI program.
os_tip_text: Keep the terminal window open as long as the detector is running. If it closes immediately, there is an error in your config.json — check carefully that you haven't forgotten any quotation marks (") or commas (,).
